method.description: Deterministic in-repository revision reconciliation across two Idaho documents with opposite defects. Each retained binary was opened and measured, and its full text was scanned for revision, version and effective-date markings — positively, to read the shield footer, and negatively, to establish that the BCI application carries none. The result was compared against the adopted edition rows, the repository asset audit and the source-acquisition queue.
method.tooling: poppler (pdfinfo, pdftotext -layout) for face text and footer reads; pdf-lib for AcroForm, annotation and page-geometry reads
method.assignmentConstraintObserved: The stop condition requires recording the shield footer as 01/01/2024, retaining BCI as REV-UNKNOWN, and never inventing an Order to Shield, and forbids downloading a binary, mutating the edition, inferring a legal conclusion, implementing a packet, enabling runtime, promoting or deploying. All observed. No order form is created, proposed or implied.

finding.headline: Two Idaho assets, two revision defects, opposite in kind. The shield petition's edition label REV-2001-01 is a parse error — the footer reads 01/01/2024 and the label took the leading 01/01 as a year and a month, moving the document twenty-three years into the past. The BCI application's REV-UNKNOWN is not a defect at all: the issuer prints no revision anywhere, so REV-UNKNOWN is the only honest value. The pairing is the point — one REV field must change and the other must be defended against a well-meant sweep.
finding.acquisitionRequiredRationale: Nothing needs to be obtained. Both binaries are retained, both were confirmed against their issuers by the completed dependency, and both revision questions are answerable from the retained bytes.

resolvedRevisions.printedFooterVerbatim: Petition to Shield Records from Public Disclosure I.C. § 67-3004(11) - 01/01/2024   Page 1 of 2
resolvedRevisions.parseErrorDiagnosis: The footer date is 01/01/2024 in MM/DD/YYYY. The recorded label REV-2001-01 is consistent with reading the leading '01/01' as YYYY-MM and discarding the true year. The result places an Idaho Clean Slate Act form — a statute enacted decades later — in January 2001, which is on its face impossible for the remedy it implements.
resolvedRevisions.whyItMattersBeyondMetadata: A twenty-three-year backdated revision would make the current form look like the oldest asset in the Idaho set and would defeat any freshness heuristic that sorts or gates on revision date. It is the kind of error that silently reverses a currentness comparison rather than merely blurring one.

resolvedRevisions.negativeFindingEvidence: An independent full-text scan of both pages of the retained bytes for revision, version and effective-date keywords, and for any date-like token, returns zero matches. The document carries no revision stamp, no version marking, no effective date and no footer date anywhere on its face. The dependency job reached the same result by the same kind of scan.
resolvedRevisions.negativeFindingQuality: This is an affirmative negative, not a failure to find. Two independent scans of the same retained bytes agree, and the document's own layout has no footer band in which a revision would sit.
resolvedRevisions.whyThisIsRecordedRatherThanLeftAlone: REV-UNKNOWN reads like a gap and invites a sweep that fills it. On the Michigan MC 227 asset resolved in the same wave, REV-UNKNOWN genuinely was a gap and three printed stamps were available to close it. Here there is nothing to read, and any value written into this field would be invented. The two cases are recorded together so the distinction cannot be lost.
resolvedRevisions.whatWouldChangeIt: Only the Idaho State Police beginning to print a revision on the form, or publishing a dated revision history for it. Neither exists today.
resolvedRevisions.doNotSubstituteAFileDate: The retained filename and any HTTP Last-Modified header are properties of a file and a server, not markings on the document. Neither may be promoted to a revision.

revUnknownIsNotOneCondition.principle: REV-UNKNOWN carries two incompatible meanings in the manifest and they must be distinguished before any sweep touches the field.

meaningOne.example: MI:MC-227, resolved in the same wave. The form prints Rev. 3/25 in three places and the repository has held the bytes that prove it all along. REV-UNKNOWN there is a metadata gap and must be closed.

revUnknownIsNotOneCondition.recommendation: The manifest would benefit from distinguishing these two states explicitly rather than expressing both as REV-UNKNOWN. Recorded as an observation for the edition owner; not applied.

orderToShieldDoesNotExist.assignedConstraint: never invent an Order to Shield
orderToShieldDoesNotExist.finding: The Idaho Supreme Court publishes no order form to accompany the Petition to Shield.
orderToShieldDoesNotExist.evidence: The dependency job established that the Clean Slate Act page carries exactly four file links — the Instructions PDF and the Petition in PDF, DOCX and RTF — with no order, stipulation or notice-of-hearing form, and that the statewide self-help forms index has no criminal or shielding category at all. The Instructions place the follow-on paper with the court: once the petition is filed, the court sets a hearing date and sends the petitioner a Notice of Hearing.
orderToShieldDoesNotExist.namedTrap: Search-engine result summaries assert that an 'Order to Shield Records from Public Disclosure' and a 'Stipulation to Shield Records from Public Disclosure' exist on courtselfhelp.idaho.gov, one of them citing a nonexistent statute. Direct retrieval of the official index pages disproves this. No order form may be added to the Idaho packet on the strength of a search summary.
orderToShieldDoesNotExist.residualUnknown: Whether individual Idaho courts nonetheless expect a petitioner to lodge a proposed order is a local-practice question that no official page answers. It stays open and is not resolved here.

documentIdAliases.consequence: The audit reports no retained Edition 1.2 asset for either component-bound id with empty candidate evidence, which reads as an acquisition gap and is not one. Both documents are retained and adopted.

Resolving both revision questions removes the reason that job cannot be scheduled, and it forecloses two opposite errors at once: writing an invented revision onto the BCI application, and leaving a twenty-three-year backdated revision on the shield petition.
implementationFamilyEffect.familyReadinessStatement: The Idaho official-PDF family remains fail-closed and this job does not move it. The revision correction has not been applied to the edition, the shield canonical path still embeds REV-2001-01, both component document-id aliases are unreconciled, generation_allowed is unchanged, runtime is disabled and no field map is built. No packet becomes generatable and no renderer is assigned.
implementationFamilyEffect.rendererObservation: Both are two-page unrotated Letter AcroForms with one-to-one field-to-widget mapping, no XFA and no encryption — 13 fields on the shield petition and 17 on the BCI application. That is the acroform_fill shape. An observation about the artifacts; no lane is assigned here.
implementationFamilyEffect.packetCompositionNote: The Idaho packet has no order form for either track, and none exists to bind. The absence is a finding, not a gap to fill.

terminalDispositionDetail.why: The narrowest disposition the evidence supports. It is not unresolved_identity: both documents, issuers, titles, roles, scopes and structures are established from the artifacts. It is not acquisition_required: both binaries are held and were confirmed against their issuers by the completed dependency. It is not a two-revision correction, because only one revision is wrong; asserting otherwise would invent a value for a document that carries none.

expectedDownstreamEffect: Idaho's Clean Slate shield petition stops carrying a revision twenty-three years earlier than the form's own printed date, and the canonical path that inherits the error is flagged for regeneration. The BCI application's REV-UNKNOWN is affirmatively defended with a reproduced negative scan, so a later currentness sweep cannot fill it with an invented value. The distinction between the two meanings of REV-UNKNOWN is recorded with a worked example on each side. The published-order-form question is closed in the negative with the specific search-summary trap named. The sole remaining open dependency of the Idaho acroform-fill job is answered. No component is rebound, no order form is created, no receipt is created, no binary enters version control, no renderer is assigned, no memo is edited, no edition is published, no packet becomes generatable, no runtime is enabled and no track changes promotion state.
